verdict.line: You lose extended poke exchanges before level 6 if you let Snip Snip! and her passive chip you from range, but you win nearly every all-in once Counter Strike punishes her Skip 'n Slash burst.

brief.thesis: Jax holds the lane and solo-kill edge (50.6% WR, 2,218 games) because his E (Counter Strike) completely no-sells the basic-attack burst Gwen generates from E (Skip 'n Slash), while her true answer to Jax's all-in — W (Hallowed Mist) — only protects her if she never has to fight back. The lane is decided by who controls the E-for-E exchange: her dash-empowered autos versus his stun-and-dodge.

theirWindow.when: she lands Skip 'n Slash and gets on-hit buff
theirWindow.what: She's about to chain empowered basic attacks for several seconds. Do not trade autos into this window — either back off or go straight into E (Counter Strike), since Counter Strike dodges all incoming basic attacks and will waste the entire buff.

yourWindow.when: her E (Skip 'n Slash) is on cooldown (13-11s)
yourWindow.what: She has no dash to disengage or refund cooldown. Leap in with Q (Leap Strike), pop W (Empower) on the strike or the following auto, and finish with E (Counter Strike) to stun and lock the trade — she cannot escape it.

start.why: The sustain and AD from Doran's Blade let you absorb Snip Snip! chip damage and still threaten trades before level 6; this path wins 57.1% over 21 games.

boots.why: Gwen's damage is entirely magic — her passive, Q, and R all scale off it — so the magic resist directly undercuts her poke and burst (63.6% WR over 11 games).

core.why: The on-hit burst spikes your Leap Strike + Empower combo hard enough to win the all-in before she can reset with Skip 'n Slash.
Gives you a shield and bonus damage tied to your empowered strikes, letting you survive her Snip Snip! poke while you close the gap.
Lets you dodge her Needlework or a follow-up burst after you've committed Counter Strike, since her ultimate still hits you through the stance.

situational.when: she is building health and her passive healing is offsetting your damage
her magic poke damage is piling up faster than you can trade back
you need wave clear to keep pace while she pokes from range

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacking attack speed compounds with your R's third-hit bonus damage, so once you're in melee range during an all-in you out-damage her on-hit empowered autos rather than trading evenly.

summoners.why: Ignite converts your measured solo-kill advantage into actual kills during the level 2-5 all-in window, and it's the highest-pickrate, best-performing pair at 74.1% pick and 55% WR.

playing.title: Save E for her E
playing.detail: Hold Counter Strike until Gwen commits Skip 'n Slash and starts her empowered auto string — it dodges every basic attack in that window and then stuns her.

playing.title: Respect Snip Snip! range
playing.detail: Her Q reaches out to 450 and ticks true damage on anyone centered in it. Stay off that range before level 6 rather than farming through it.

playing.title: Don't dive the mist
playing.detail: Hallowed Mist makes her untargetable from outside it, but entering exposes both of you. Only walk in when your full Q-W-E combo is ready to end the fight.

playing.title: Engage on her E cooldown
playing.detail: Skip 'n Slash is her only escape. When it's down (13-11s cooldown), leap in — she cannot disengage your stun.

playing.title: Buy Mercury's Treads first back
playing.detail: Every source of her damage is magic, so the MR cuts both her poke and her passive sustain simultaneously.

playing.title: Hunt the level 2 all-in
playing.detail: Jax holds the solo-kill edge in this matchup. Punish her for stepping up to poke with Q before she has Hallowed Mist available at 6.

playing.title: Don't contest open poke late
playing.detail: Her R cooldown falls to 8.5/8s at rank 4-5, letting her zone constantly from 1200 range. Play around wave state instead of standing in the open past level 16.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and win-rate figures are measured from real games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning — why the E-for-E exchange decides the lane — is my own read on the ability interactions, not sampled data.
